builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DyNA-Mixer: Decoupling Time and Topology for Scalable Dynamic Node Affinity Prediction
summary: DyNA-Mixer replaces monolithic temporal graph networks that jointly model time and structure for dynamic link/affinity prediction with a decoupled design: a multi-scale temporal predictor, a query-time Virtual Collaborative Graph for collaborative signals, and a gated residual fusion, plus sparsity-aware evaluation that scores only recently active pairs. The cost is a more complex multi-component pipeline to implement and maintain, and forecasting cost that still scales with the number of recently active source-destination pairs, which can be large in dense recommender or transaction graphs. It can fail when transferred off the four TGB benchmark datasets: reported gains are benchmark-specific, the virtual graph's inferred relationships may not hold in domains with sparse or noisy interaction histories, and the paper provides no evidence on inference latency or memory footprint under production serving constraints.
rationale: The method targets a specialized temporal-graph ranking problem and is only worth evaluating if the reader already operates continuous-time interaction data in production, which the constrained-infrastructure profile does not establish.
